facts.activity_file: responding to slope-radar and prism alarms

control_failures.control_label: benching, battering or shoring of an excavation
inspection and monitoring of highwalls and batters

hazard_media: stored potential of an elevated component
facts.site: Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop
facts.title: gravity release during routine operation on EX-9101

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was medical treatment injury, with 1 person injured.

defences.finding: Control EXCAVATION_SUPPORT: the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent, and the learning team review classified this as an organisational factor.
Control GROUND_CONDITION_INSPECTION: the inspection and monitoring of highwalls and batters was not in place, and the learning team review classified this as an organisational factor.
Control SLOPE_MONITORING_RESPONSE: the response to slope monitoring alarms was never verified as effective, and the learning team review classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the response to slope monitoring alarms on EX-9101 and record the assurance activity before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in monitoring and inspecting ground conditions, specifically responding to slope-radar and prism alarms. EX-9101 (earthmoving fleet) is in service for loading and dozing. The task proceeded during routine operation while the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent. The gravity energy involved is held as suspended load, and the recorded presentation was fall, collapse, crush.
response.summary: On 4 January 2026 an incident occurred on EX-9101 at Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop during routine operation, releasing gravity energy held as suspended load.
